finding.reasons: OSM-flagged malicious repository (severity CRITICAL) [DPRK (North Korea) (per OSM)]: DPRK Contagious Interview campaign using VS Code tasks.json. Auto-executes malicious payload when VS Code opens folder via runOn: folderOpen trigger or .githook | Tier-2 confirmed (bash score 5)

osm_report.threat_description:
VS Code autorun dropper. Payload in .vscode/tasks.json.
Outbound: fetch-and-run. It downloads code from coreviewer.vercel.app and executes it (.vscode/tasks.json).
Runs automatically when the folder is opened in VS Code (hidden folderOpen task that fetches and runs a remote script).
Matches PolinRider / Contagious Interview (DPRK): fake-recruiter coding tasks that run a downloader when opened in VS Code. Payload host: coreviewer.vercel.app.
Campaign GW-C-a3717cc8: one of 20 confirmed repos across 17 accounts sharing the dropper URL shape task/{os}?token=. Payload served from 10 distinct hosts, including codeviewer-three.vercel.app, coreviewer.vercel.app, jerryfox-platform.vercel.app, task-hrec.vercel.app, thopywork.vercel.app.
Attribution: we assess this repository as PROBABLE North Korea 'Contagious Interview' activity. Signals: Delivery vector matches Contagious-Interview tradecraft: vscode-folderopen-autorun; Payload host is curated known-DPRK / Contagious-Interview infrastructure: coreviewer.vercel.app; Corroboration (not counted toward attribution): OSM/news already names dprk (north korea).
Confirmed by static analysis; the code was read, never executed.
osm_report.payload_description:
Malicious payload found in: .vscode/tasks.json
- Outbound: fetch-and-run. It downloads code from coreviewer.vercel.app and executes it (.vscode/tasks.json).
- .vscode/tasks.json: VS Code task with runOn: folderOpen; runs the moment the folder is opened, no install or click needed
- Attacker hosts: coreviewer.vercel.app
